## Great Britain

GB joins the markets you can pick, as the thirty-fourth price zone. Prices,
CO2, the plans and the windows all work the way they do everywhere else.

Three things are different, and it is better to read them here than to
discover them on the dashboard.

**Prices are in pence.** Great Britain is the only market whose prices are
published in its own currency instead of being converted from euro: the
day-ahead arrives as GBP per MWh and is served as `GBP/kWh`. The sensors say
so, and a retail formula is typed in pence. Nothing needs to be set for this.

**There is no measured forecast quality yet.** Quality is judged over a
rolling thirty days, and the British forecasts started in October. Until the
window fills, the two quality sensors stay empty and the combined score is
carried by price and CO2 alone. Every market went through this; it is a
warm-up, not a fault.

**There is no retail estimate**, as for Switzerland and the Italian zones.
The own retail formula works, and time-of-day grid charges can be entered by
hand from your supplier's rates.

## Updating from 1.15.x

Nothing changes for existing entries. GB appears in the market list when you
add a new one.
